set.approach: Park at the pullout for the fifth bridge on the Maligne Lake Road and walk across the bridge, then turn left into the forest toward the sixth bridge. After a minute or so turn right onto trail 7H and climb a steep hill. Where 7H bears right, take the unmarked trail on the left and follow it through open Douglas fir forest. When you see a drop-off on your left you are close: turn right and downhill for the Rock Gardens (continuing left leads to the Boulder Gardens). The route is immediately left of the dihedral where Green Piton begins.

set.approach: Park at the Hidden Valley lot on Highway 16 (large pullout with an outhouse) and take the Hidden Valley trail from the east end of the lot, crossing a small pond that is usually bridged with logs. The trail braids into goat trails and turns up into the valley. A rock cage (gabion) with an orange circular sign marks the turn; follow orange flagging, gabions and cairns uphill to the foot of the Syncline cliff. The first routes are on the first buttress. Continue along the cliff base past the first major break, to the first bolt line on the face of the second buttress: look for a slab with a small roof partway up, with a patch of broken rock beside it on the left.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route as far as the second pitch, then down to a treed ledge that has its own rappel anchors. With a long rope one rappel reaches the tree ledge, skipping the second-pitch anchors; with a shorter rope, stop at those anchors for one more rappel. From the ledge, walk a short way climber's right to a separate set of anchors that reach the ground. All anchors have rap rings.

review.notes: Route page for the start and descent; Syncline page for parking and trail. Distances and times left out.

set.approach: Take Highway 93A south from Jasper, past Athabasca Falls, to Leech Lake and park at the pullout or at the small one a little further on the left. A good trail leads through the forest to the crag. Continue beyond sector 1 and through sector 2, which has one bolted route. Sector 3 lies in a broad talus field where the trees on your right have ended, with the main wall on your left. Altered Beast is at the right end of the main wall, beginning in a small left-facing feature.

review.notes: Lost Boys and sector pages for approach; route page for position.

set.approach: Park in the small pullout on Highway 16 east of Jasper that has a characteristic gate at its back. Follow the creek bed, using the faint trail on the left bank, which is easier and safer than threading the boulders in the creek. The trail passes sand towers on the right, then drops into a small canyon; the limestone underfoot is polished by water and slick. The cliff appears soon after the canyon ends. A 64 is the rightmost line on the face, above a pair of trees that stand just left of the broken gully.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for position on the face. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Hidden Valley lot on Highway 16, walk toward the park gates along the lot's edge to find the trail that crosses the pond and climbs a relatively steep hill (if you are beside the highway you have gone too far). The trail flattens, braids and heads up a slope into Hidden Valley. Follow the main trail to the ladder, climb it, stay on the main trail and bear left at forks. Soon after the First Wall, a good trail scrambles up the slope; where it levels out, follow the foot of the cliff band that rises on your right, until a steep blank slab appears with a conspicuous left-facing corner at its right-hand end. The route is a bolt line beginning immediately left of the big corner, then angling into it and onto steeper rock.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for position.
